gao-gaoreports-gao-08-239t: GAO took its Medicaid tax-cheat findings to Congress in 2007. The probe had matched care providers' pay records against tax files and found thousands who billed the health plan while owing back taxes. The hearing put one sharp question to Congress: why should public health dollars flow to firms that skip out on their own tax bills?
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-249t: This 2007 Government Accountability Office testimony addresses damages owed to seven Native American tribes whose reservations were harmed by dams on the Missouri River. Decades after federal flood-control projects flooded tribal land, compensation questions lingered. GAO lays out the history of the damages and the status of efforts to make the affected tribes whole.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-229t: In 2007 testimony, the Government Accountability Office weighed whether to extend a demonstration project on service members' employment-rights claims. The pilot tested new ways to resolve disputes when returning troops said employers violated their reemployment rights. GAO lays out considerations for Congress: what the project showed, what it cost, and whether the experiment deserved more time.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-199t: This 2007 Government Accountability Office testimony urges HUD to streamline its processes so project-based rental assistance payments go out on time. Landlords housing low-income tenants under federal contracts were waiting too long for their money. GAO's findings connect bureaucratic delays to real consequences: when payments lag, affordable-housing providers suffer and tenants' stability is put at risk.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-119t: GAO told Congress in 2007 that the brains running power plants, waterworks, and factories were coming under guard — but the guard was patchy. Many shield projects were rolling, yet big holes stayed open. The briefing warns that the machines of daily life were getting hackable faster than the nation was learning to lock them down.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-139t: GAO told Congress in 2007 that Homeland Security had toughened the skies since 9/11 — better screens, tighter cargo rules — yet key weak spots held on. The briefing gives credit for the climb while pointing at the rungs still missing. For flyers, the takeaway was mixed: safer than before, still not safe enough.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1259t: GAO asked Congress in 2007 about an untapped flu-fighting asset: the city-level boards that link federal offices town by town. Could these local webs help keep government humming if a bad flu swept the workforce? The briefing sizes up a sleeper player in outbreak planning — the neighborhood ties between far-flung federal shops.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1249t: Another 2007 Government Accountability Office update on the Capitol Visitor Center, reporting schedule and cost status as of September 25, 2007. The underground complex beneath the Capitol kept slipping and growing more expensive. The testimony adds another entry to the project's long record of overruns — a case study in how federal construction projects go wrong under Congress's own nose.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1229t: GAO carried its responder-health findings into a hearing room in 2007, pressing Congress face to face. Sick Ground Zero workers needed screening that actually reached them, the testimony argued — not programs on paper. The hearing added urgency to the paper trail: real people, real illnesses, still waiting.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1079t: Rebuilding the Gulf Coast would cost the feds plenty — GAO's 2007 briefing lays out the money stakes for Congress. The testimony tallies the federal exposure in the post-Katrina rebuild. The findings frame the recovery as a fiscal saga, not just a construction job.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1149t: The Capitol's basement boondoggle marched on in 2007 — GAO's July briefing logs more months, more millions on the Visitor Center. The testimony is another verse in the project's long ballad of delay. Congress's own construction job kept teaching the same lesson: megaprojects mock their budgets.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1089t: The watchdogs needed sharper teeth in 2007 — GAO's briefing says inspectors general deserved more independence and accountability. The testimony makes the case for freeing the auditors to audit. The findings argue that a watchdog on a short leash is a pet, not a guard.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1099t: The weather eyes in orbit were aging in 2007 — GAO's briefing tracks the wins and worries in buying the next environmental satellites. The testimony balances progress against the risks. The findings warn that the storm warnings depend on hardware with a shelf life.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1039t: A German base project went off the rails in 2007 — GAO's briefing details the mismanagement of the Kaiserslautern military community center. The testimony is a case study in overseas construction gone wrong. The findings show distance from Washington did not mean distance from waste.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1049t: Africa's aid compacts were a mixed bag in 2007 — GAO's briefing tracks the Millennium Challenge Corporation's progress and snags across the continent. The testimony pairs hope with homework for lawmakers watching the money. The findings measure big development bets against ground-level reality.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-989t: Abroad, women and low-skill workers got a better deal in 2007 — GAO's briefing surveys foreign efforts to pull them into lasting work. The testimony shops for transferable wins worth copying at home. The findings suggest America's labor ladder could use some imported rungs.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-719t: The tax agency's budget pitch got a full hearing in 2007 — GAO's briefing grades the IRS's 2008 request alongside its 2007 scorecard. The testimony links dollars requested to deeds delivered for Congress. The findings ask the bottom-line question: did the collector earn its keep?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-859t: Workers were being mislabeled as contractors in 2007 — GAO's briefing says better outreach could fix the classification mess for good. The testimony targets the payroll dodge hurting workers nationwide. The findings defend the paycheck with a simple rule: call a worker a worker.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-819t: Crop insurance integrity needed steady tending in 2007 — GAO's briefing repeats the call for cleaner books and saner program costs. The testimony keeps the pressure on the farm agency. The findings' refrain: the farm safety net should catch farmers, not fraud.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-799t: The missile-defense budget was a fog in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the agency's flexibility hid the program's true costs from Congress. The testimony demands clearer numbers and honest accounting. The findings warn that freedom to spend is not freedom from ever having to account.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-779t: The 2010 census design was gelling in 2007 — GAO's briefing says progress showed, but tech buys, temp hiring, and the Gulf region all needed managing. The testimony lists the pressure points one by one. The findings warn that the count's weak links were already visible years out.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-489t: The Coast Guard's budget and overhaul got a hearing in 2007 — GAO's briefing reviews the service's spending plans, performance, and reorganization. The testimony takes the full measure. The findings ask whether the guardians of the coast were funded to match their mission.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-649t: The next air-traffic system kept inching along in 2007 — GAO's briefing reviews the progress made and the planning headaches ahead. The testimony takes stock of the whole effort. The findings warn that the transformation of the skies needed steadier hands.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-639t: Securing Iraq's loose weapons was the hard lesson of 2007, and GAO's briefing says the Pentagon should finally apply what it learned. The testimony repeats the plea with real urgency for Congress. The findings' refrain is blunt: guard the arsenals, or you will end up arming the insurgency.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-599t: The FDA's drug-safety watch was still blurry in 2007 — GAO's briefing says the agency had to fix its postmarket decision-making. The testimony repeats the prescription. The findings argue that the pill bottle's fine print is a matter of life and death.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-589t: Wounded warriors were navigating a broken handoff in 2007, and GAO's briefing again traces the recovery challenges injured troops faced. The testimony repeats the indictment with force. The findings demand the system honor the sacrifice with competent care. The wounded deserved better than the wait.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-499t: The visitor-tracking system was falling short in 2007, and GAO's briefing says US-VISIT had not met expectations amid long-standing management troubles. The testimony lists the failures. The findings warn that the border's digital eye was half-blind. The digital eye needed new glasses.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-459t: Passenger trains were soft targets in 2007, and GAO's briefing says a federal strategy with better coordination was needed to guide security. The testimony demands the plan. The findings warn that the rails carried millions with too little guarding. The rails deserved a real shield.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-449t: The food-safety system earned the high-risk label in 2007, and GAO's briefing says the designation could focus attention on the fragmented watch. The testimony makes the case. The findings argue that dinner should not be a gamble. The dinner table deserved a real watchdog.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-439t: The Army's gear-rebuild plan got an early look in 2007, and GAO's briefing offers preliminary notes on the reset strategies. The testimony previews the findings. The findings warn that the worn-out equipment needed a real plan, not just patches. The reset had to be more than a rinse.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-389t: Deficits mattered in 2007, and GAO's briefing says saving the future required tough choices in the present. The testimony delivers the hard math. The findings warn that the red ink was a mortgage on the unborn. The choices could not wait for a better decade.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-369t: Oil royalty giveaways were costing billions in 2007, and GAO's briefing says the relief would likely cost the government dearly, with the final tally unknown. The testimony does the math. The findings warn that the public's oil was being sold at a discount. The giveaway had to be counted.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-359t: The Pentagon's services buying spree needed a leash in 2007, and GAO's briefing says the department had to exert management and oversight. The testimony demands the control. The findings warn that the service contracts were the budget's blind spot. The spending needed supervision.
